A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EEG participant-diversity study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original scaling experiments with TCN, mAtt, and LaBraM on three EEG tasks, augmentation and pre-training evaluations, and a preprocessing ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds a contiguous-sampling control and statistical analysis of augmentation gains.

M1.justification: The architectures, training objectives, augmentation transformations and parameter ranges, and LaBraM fine-tuning procedure are retained. Contiguous subsampling is introduced only as an experimental control.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TUAB normality prediction, CAUEEG dementia diagnosis, and PhysioNet sleep staging using the same represented datasets and tasks. The new sampling control uses existing TUAB coverage; additional datasets discussed in related work are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The evaluated model and augmentation sets remain TCN, mAtt, LaBraM, AmplitudeScaling, FrequencyShift, and PhaseRandomisation, with the same pre-training and preprocessing comparisons. Newly discussed foundation models and excluded augmentations do not become evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix A.7 adds a TUAB/TCN control drawing consecutive segments from a randomly selected starting index, alongside uniform subsampling. Existing experimental settings remain unchanged. Newly specified split provenance and PhysioNet stratification document existing experiments rather than establish changed splits.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused control testing whether uniform sampling artificially increases segment diversity, and an analysis of whether augmentation gains depend on sample size (Appendices A.7 and A.9). The sampling control covers one model and task; the original LaBraM preprocessing ablation is retained.

E5.justification: Table 2 introduces Spearman correlations, uncorrected p-values, and a Bonferroni-correction qualification. Figure 7 reports the new control over five seeds with standard errors. Existing experiments retain their previously reported seed counts and uncertainty practices.

E6.justification: All eleven original figure plots and Table 1 learning rates are unchanged. New Figure 7 reports similar scaling patterns under uniform and contiguous sampling. New Table 2 includes, for example, CAUEEG/TCN/FrequencyShift rho=-0.430 with uncorrected p=0.018; no reported correlation survives Bonferroni correction.

T1.justification: The hierarchical participant-distribution model, empirical and population risk definitions, and generalization-rate arguments are unchanged. v2 combines v1's two displayed risk equations into Equation 1 without adding mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract's scientific claims and central contributions remain the same: distinguish participant count from sample size, establish task-dependent scaling, and assess augmentation and pre-training benefits. The four explicit research questions, answers, and new conclusion largely restate these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 expands the applicability discussion to distinguish generalization to unseen participants from participant-specific BCI models. It develops earlier label-preservation caveats into explanations for augmentation results and adds the possibility that training data already supplies sufficient amplitude and frequency invariances. Appendix A.7 newly discusses sampling realism.

D1.justification: v2 adds split provenance, PhysioNet age/sex stratification, GPU types, runtime estimates, software dependencies, and dataset access or licensing information. The research-code link was already present. Some details are removed, including explicit channel lists and the statement that the best checkpoint is restored after early stopping.

R1.justification: The new Related Work section substantially develops positioning against Banville's and Kiessner's scaling studies, emphasizing unseen-participant generalization and separate control of participants and segments. Foundation-model coverage is revised to include BIOT, EEGFormer, CBraMod, and EEGPT, while earlier discussions citing MAEEG, Neuro-GPT, and EEG Conformer are removed.

P1.justification: v2 places Methods before Results, organizes results around four explicit questions and answers, and introduces separate Related Work, Limitations and Future Work, and Conclusion sections. Model comparison and substantial training/statistical documentation move into reorganized appendices. This materially changes the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The document adopts NeurIPS formatting with redesigned title and author blocks, typography, margins, and figure sizing and placement. Original appendix figures are reordered and regrouped, and Table 1 moves into the appendix. Figure 7 and Table 2 are new displays; the original plots themselves are retained.

improvement.justification: The new sampling control addresses a realistic concern about the original design, while Table 2 directly examines augmentation gains across sample sizes. Expanded research positioning and reproducibility information improve transparency. These are useful but bounded gains around unchanged main experiments; they outweigh small losses of implementation detail, such as omitted channel lists and checkpoint-restoration wording.
